introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde imprime « ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS » (4 sur 6 questions imprimées), sans section et sans mention « only the first four will be marked ». `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers.

Sujet scanné de 3 pages (page de garde, questions 1 à 4, questions 5 et 6), lu en image ; aucun schéma ni figure imprimé, donc `figures` vide dans tous les fichiers. Filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignorés. L'en-tête imprimé « Food And Nutrition 2 » est recopié en « Food and Nutrition 2 » dans l'introduction.

Points : chaque question imprime « Total = (25 marks) » ; les points imprimés des sous-questions totalisent bien 25 pour chacune des 6 questions (aucun écart). Pour 2(a), 5(a) et 6(b), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des parties (i) et (ii) imprimées (2+5, 2+5, 3+5).

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au nombre exact d'éléments demandés. D'autres réponses sont valables pour les questions de liste ; le barème d'un point par élément est une hypothèse (le sujet ne le détaille pas). Aucune teneur nutritive chiffrée n'est avancée, sauf l'énergie d'un gramme de lipide (environ 37 kJ, valeur du programme).

Question 1(e) « mechanical raising agents » : le programme n'en nomme usuellement que deux (l'air et la vapeur), le sujet en demande quatre. Le corrigé donne quatre procédés mécaniques distincts (air par tamisage, par crémage, par fouettage, et vapeur) ; d'autres manuels répondent autrement (battage, pliage, laminage). À relire par un enseignant de Food and Nutrition.

Faits de cours à relire par un enseignant : les objectifs alimentaires de 5(b) (le sujet n'en impose aucun), les causes de faible production de 5(c) et les points de 6(d) sont des listes de manuel ; plusieurs autres réponses seraient acceptées.

Fautes d'impression du sujet recopiées telles quelles : « five (5) importance » au singulier (1d, 2a ii, 2d, 4d), « (5marks) », « (8marks) », « Recall three (3) advantages », « Pick out three (3) advantages ... of microwave cooking » sans point final, « Outline three (3) advantages and two (2) disadvantages of boiling » sans point final, « Define invitation ».

questions.enonce_markdown:
i. Define food preservation.

(2 marks)

ii. Outline five (5) importance of food preservation.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**i. Definition (2 marks).** Food preservation is the treatment of food (for example by cooling, drying, smoking, salting, canning or freezing) to stop or slow down its spoilage by micro-organisms and enzymes, so that it can be kept safe to eat for a longer time.

**ii. Five importance of food preservation (1 mark each).**

1. **It prevents food from spoiling**, so less food is wasted and money is saved.
2. **It makes food available all the year round**, including out of season, when the food is scarce.
3. **It keeps food safe**, because the growth of the micro-organisms that cause food poisoning is stopped or slowed.
4. **It allows the surplus of a good harvest to be stored** and used in time of shortage or famine.
5. **It allows food to be transported over long distances and sold** in markets far from where it was produced, and it gives variety to the diet (for example smoked fish, dried meat).

(Other correct point: some nutrients and the flavour of the food are kept.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Recall three (3) advantages and three (3) disadvantages of fast food.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Fast food** is food that is quickly prepared and served ready to eat, for example fried chicken, chips, burgers, pizza and snacks bought at a roadside stall or restaurant.

| Advantages (3 marks) | Disadvantages (3 marks) |
|---|---|
| 1. It is **quick to get**, so it saves time for busy people (workers, students, travellers). | 1. It is usually **high in fat, salt, sugar and energy** and low in fibre and vitamins, so a diet based on it is not balanced and may lead to overweight and heart disease. |
| 2. It is **convenient**: no shopping, cooking or washing-up are needed, and it is easy to find. | 2. It may be **prepared in unhygienic conditions** (dirty hands, re-used oil, food kept uncovered), which can cause food poisoning. |
| 3. It gives a **variety** of ready-to-eat dishes and it is often not expensive for a single meal. | 3. It is **more expensive than home cooking** when eaten regularly for a whole family, and the packaging causes litter and waste. |

questions.enonce_markdown:
Name five (5) guidelines to observe when buying a freezer.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five guidelines to observe when buying a freezer (1 mark each):

1. **Size (capacity)** - choose a size that suits the number of people in the family and the quantity of food to be stored.
2. **Type and space available** - choose a chest or an upright freezer according to the space in the house or kitchen.
3. **Running cost** - choose a model that uses little electricity (energy efficient).
4. **Price and budget** - compare prices and buy what the family can afford.
5. **Make, guarantee and after-sales service** - buy a reliable make with a guarantee, and one for which repairs and spare parts are available.

(Other correct points: a good thermostat or temperature control, ease of cleaning and defrosting, a lock, baskets or shelves, and the noise made by the machine.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline five (5) importance of a balanced diet.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **balanced diet** is a diet that contains all the nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, mineral salts, water and fibre) in the right quantities for the needs of the person. Five importance (1 mark each):

1. **It supplies the energy** needed for work, play and body activities.
2. **It promotes growth and the repair of worn-out or damaged body tissues.**
3. **It protects the body against diseases**, because vitamins and mineral salts keep the body's defences strong.
4. **It prevents deficiency diseases and malnutrition** (for example rickets, anaemia, kwashiorkor).
5. **It helps to keep a healthy body weight** and gives good health, mental alertness and a long, active life.

questions.enonce_markdown:
List two (2) sources of animal protein and two of plant protein.

(2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
(Half a mark for each correct source.)

| Animal protein | Plant protein |
|---|---|
| 1. Meat (beef, goat meat, chicken) | 1. Beans (cowpeas) |
| 2. Fish (or eggs, milk, cheese) | 2. Groundnuts (or soya beans, peas) |
